recipes.name: Johnsonville Italian Meatballs
ingredients_raw: 1 (19 ounce) package Johnsonville® Italian Mild Sausage Links, casings removed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine bread crumbs, egg, Parmesan cheese, milk, and onion in a large bowl. Add sausage to bread crumb mixture; mix well. Shape into 20 meatballs and place them on a shallow baking pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until meatballs are cooked through, about 20 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of a meatball should read at least 160 degrees F (72 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Johnsonville Italian Meatballs

author.name: From the Kitchen at Johnsonville Sausage

raw_recipe.description: These Italian sausage meatballs flavored with Parmesan and onion bake in just 20 minutes and are a delicious way to jazz up your pasta night suppers.

review.reviewBody: I like to make this recipe for two different recipes; Meatball Subs with homemade marinara and Barbeque Meatballs. This comes together quickly with ingredients most people have on hand. Sometimes, I'll throw in garlic/onion powder and italian seasoning. They hold together well and don't get mushy when left to hang out in whatever sauce you add them to. NOTE: This can be made healthier with ground turkey or chicken and spiced up to make taste like ground pork with brown sugar, sage, red pepper flake, marjoram, fresh ground pepper and a little salt. Fools my husband every time.

I have never had any meatballs that were 100% Italian sausage usually they've either been ground beef or a combination of Italian sausage and ground beef. I chose to cook these meatballs in my instant pot - I cheated by pouring Bertolli spaghetti sauce over the meatballs, along with 1/3 cup water, and cooked them on low pressure for 12 minutes before doing a quick release! I served these meatballs with homemade pasta. Semi-homemade dinner in under 20 minutes start to finish!!!

I doubled this recipe since I'm cooking for 7 big eaters. I left out onion (allergies) added 1 tsp. Italian herb blend, 2 cloves garlic. I forgot to add milk, but I'm cooking them in the crockpot, so I don't need extra liquid. Topping with homemade Italian sauce in crockpot to make meatball sandwiches on ciabatta rolls (with provolone of course.)

These were great. I used ground venison instead of sausage (we don't like sausage). Made 33, baked in a pan, put the cooked meat balls on a couple of cookie sheets; put in freezer til frozen; added all to a gallon freezer zip lock bag and used as needed. These are delicious right out of the freezer, simmered in your favorite spaghetti sauce and you have a delicious meal within 20 minutes. Add a salad and Texas toast. Umm

This is super easy and very tasty! I was going to buy ready-made meatballs from the store for a party, but I came across this. I took a leap of faith and made 4 recipes at once (using my Kitchen Aid mixer to mix all the ingredients). I used 2 Italian sausage packages, 1 lb ground turkey and 1 lb ground beef. I used onion powder instead of onions. They came out amazing. 4 recipes made about 120 meatballs. My kids ate them first for dinner and they love the meatballs. Thank you for a great recipe!

Oh yah, I made this great recipe for an Italian hero and my family raved about them! The meatballs were delicious, I made them a little large so needed 30 minutes for cook time. I took them out and placed them on the bottom of the roll and threw on a slice of provolone on top then put them under the broiler for 2 minutes. Perfect!

I added a pound of hamburg with the sweet Italian sausage. I doubled other ingredients and added garlic and fresh basil. I love meatballs on pasta or in a grinder roll with sauce and cheese. I think it helps if you flour and brown them before you bake.

I’ve made these meatballs too many times to count. I use bulk sweet Italian (sometimes mixed with hot Italian}. Lately I’ve been making this low-carb/keto by substituting 1/4 cup finely ground blanched almond flour for the breadcrumbs. Use grated (not powdered) parmesan, 1/2 & 1/2 for milk. I always add extra seasoning: s&p, fennel seeds, garlic, Italian seasoning, red pepper flakes, oregano…You really can’t screw this up!

These meatballs were fabulous! They were so tender and so flavorful! I added one clove of minced garlic and used Italian seasoned Panko breadcrumbs (that's what I had on hand). I flipped the meatballs halfway through the cooking time and they were perfect! Hubby has requested this recipe for our meatballs going forward!

These were fantastic! Changes I made: used turkey sausage as this is what we had in the freezer, used very finely crushed saltines as we were out of breadcrumbs, increased saltines to 1/2 c as the mixture was a bit too goopy to form a proper meatball, threw in some fresh garlic, garlic powder, a liberal amount of red pepper flakes cuz we like things spicy, a dusting of ground oregano and a few crushed fennel seeds. I made 16 balls out of this so had to bake about 30 minutes, til they were nice and brown on their bottoms :) and oozing melted parmesan. The texture and consistency of the finished product was great, tender yet firm enough to withstand simmering in a red gravy, or even a bbq sauce if you care to change up the sausage flavor/seasoning a bit. I served these with penne and roasted tomatoes and roasted hot Italian garlic with crumbled feta cheese and fresh chopppd basil from my potted Globe. They were a bit hit with my family.

These meatballs are really good. I added a pound of ground chuck to the Italian sausage and some oregano. I didn't put them in a sauce. Instead I just put them over thin spaghetti noodles with some shredded parmesan cheese and garlic bread. Delicious!

A decent, simple recipe. However, green can cheese (regardless of brand) is NEVER 100% parm, and is sucks. For GOOD meatballs, use DOP parm. reggiano or Grana padano, and grate it fresh yourself if possible. It takes the meatball up a notch or two. Half sausage/half ground beef... another notch or two!
There's one missing. I cooked them in a cast iron skillet in the oven. Turned out great.

Made exactly per recipe. Baked for 20 min; interior temperature was 180 after that, but didn't seem at all overcooked. Very tasty. Outside of meatball had a very slight crunch to it; inside was tender.

These were very easy and quick to make, and the recipe is easily "tweaked". (I didn't have any milk and my roommate doesn't like onions, so I used a couple of tablespoons of cottage cheese and a little water, and left the onions out completely). I also substituted garlic and herb breadcrumbs for plain. My only complaint is that they didn't brown in the oven, even when they were cooked to temp.
Made this recipe, didn't change anything. They were delicious!!! My family ate them without anything on them, just plain old meatballs, and they were a hit.
I like these meatballs however they burnt a little on the bottom but they are very delicious
These are by far the best meatballs I have ever made. I get compliments on them every time I make them.
